description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 1 round 1, 2026-09-13).  t/op/hash.t: P 494/0, C 8/7 -- 479 rows short, the fourth-biggest early-stopper outside re/ + uni/.

MEASURED (PCL_SUITE_KEEP): ONE aborted top-level form.
  ; PCL recovery: top-level form aborted (recovered):
      Can't locate loadable object for module this module in @INC
The file then reaches `done_testing()` having run 15 rows; perl runs 494.

THE SITE is t/op/hash.t:137 inside `sub validate_hash`:
    require Hash::Util;
    sub Hash::Util::bucket_ratio (\%);
    my $ratio = Hash::Util::bucket_ratio(%$h);
`validate_hash` is called by `torture_hash`, which is called ~30 times at the top level with large key sets -- that is where the other 479 rows live.

CAUSE: Hash::Util is an XS module (Hash/Util/Util.so); PCL's core-shim require fallback finds the .pm but no loadable object, so the require dies and takes the enclosing top-level form with it.  `bucket_ratio` returns "used/total" for the hash's bucket array -- a readout of perl's INTERNAL hash representation, which PCL does not have (it has CL hash tables).

VERDICT PROPOSED: this is the "measures perl internals" class (s473t1's verdict class; DECIDED s397 ruled there is NO separate suite verdict for it -- one citable docs/not-supported.md section instead).  The honest cause for the 479 rows is therefore a not-supported entry ("Hash::Util::bucket_ratio and the hash bucket array" under the internals section), NOT a fix.  What IS fixable and is not this task: `require`-ing an XS module whose .pm exists should behave like perl's "Can't locate loadable object" with the MODULE NAME in it -- PCL's message says "module this module", which is how the census could not attribute it by grep.

ALSO NOTE the message bug: "Can't locate loadable object for module this module in @INC" -- the interpolation of the module name is broken in the shim's die text.  Cheap fix, own filler.
subject: op/hash.t: `require Hash::Util` aborts the form that holds every torture_hash row -- 479 of 494 rows lost to one missing XS module
